newsitem.title: TURKEY: Reuters poll sees higher Turkish May inflation.
newsitem.headline: Reuters poll sees higher Turkish May inflation.

text.p: A Reuters poll showed that Turkey's monthly May inflation data, due on Wednesday, would be higher than last year's levels.

Poll results, based on predictions of 10 banks, four brokerage houses and two economists, showed estimates for consumer price inflation centered around 5.5-6 percent while wholesale price predictions focused at 5-5.5 percent levels.
Turkey's monthly consumer price inflation was 4.5 percent and wholesale inflation 4.1 percent in May 1996.

The lowest and highest forecasts for the consumer prices were 4.2 percent and 6.5 percent respectively, and 4.0 percent and 6.2 percent for wholesale prices. May Consumer Price Inflation Number of Estimates
May Wholesale Price Inflation Number of Estimates
Analysts also expect monthly inflation to run above last year's levels in coming months.

"Some public price hikes are still being held. Oil prices were raised on the last day of May which will not be shown in May inflation. Hopes for lower inflation in summer months depending on the seasonal factors have faded," said a securities analyst.
Analysts also say any possible early election would also fuel inflation. The government unveiled its plan on Sunday to call for snap elections. No specific date has been set yet.
But economists say Turkey should hold elections as soon as possible to ease its negative effects on the economy and inflation.

"Nearest the date for early elections, less the impact over inflation... Delayed price adjustments in the aftermath of elections will raise the inflation figures," said Faruk Selcuk, an associate professor of economics at Bilkent University.
